column6: Bullet on Goldstone counting (ferromagnet one k^2 branch) is correct but contradicted the older Explainer; Explainer fixed, see old:ex

Explainer said number of Goldstone bosons always equals number of broken generators; false for ferromagnets. Restricted to Lorentz-invariant systems and antiferromagnet-type cases, ferromagnet named as exception
Same unqualified one-mode-per-generator counting rule; qualified to Lorentz-invariant systems, ferromagnet exception added

Bullet 2 correction claimed only a gas recently out of a low-entropy state retraces its path on reversal; under exact reversal every gas retraces its own past (and the Explainer says a just-equilibrated gas does). Rewrote: reversal retraces the past, a long-equilibrated gas first retraces equilibrium states and tiny disturbances block going further back
Worked: k_F=(3pi^2 n)^(1/3), <eps>=3/5 E_F, P=2/3 U/V, copper E_F=7.05 eV
Explainer said (3/5)N E_F is roughly 60% of (3/2)N k_B T_F; ratio is 0.4. Changed to 40%
Worked: F_min=f0-alpha^2/4beta, jump a^2 T_c/2beta, chi ratio 2
Explainer stated the Ginzburg criterion as correlation length small compared to atomic scales; replaced with fluctuations of m in a correlation volume small compared to m^2
Dropped qualifier: correlations fall as e^(-r/xi)/r only in three dimensions; added "in three dimensions". Cubic-term first-order condition a=w^2/4b checked
Dropped qualifier: MSD ~ (k_BT/m)t^2 at short times needs averaging over thermal initial velocities (fixed v0 gives v0^2 t^2); added
Dropped qualifier: Curie law chi=N mu^2/kT holds for two-state spins with moment +-mu; classical vector moments give N mu^2/3kT. Added "two-state ... +-mu"
Spin-1/2 commutator gives theta(t) sin(w0 t) tanh(hbar w0/2kT), checked
Quantum factor (1-e^(-hbar w/kT))/2hbar reduces to w/2kT classically, checked
Bullet 2 called power-law decay at critical points quasi-long-range order; that term belongs to the 2D XY low-T phase. Reworded to keep the two cases separate
